title: Prospective Dynamics of Bullying Perpetration and Bullying Victimization in Adolescents: A Two-Wave Cross-Lagged Network Analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bullying perpetration and victimization frequently co-occur in adolescence, yet research relying on aggregate measures provides limited insight into how specific behaviors and experiences are prospectively connected. This study uses a network perspective to examine the transitivity, persistency, and centrality underlying the longitudinal overlap between bullying perpetration and victimization.
METHODS: Data were collected from a public high school in China using a two-wave design in 2023. The final sample included 438 adolescents (mean age = 16.53 years; 39.3% girls). Bullying perpetration (nine items) and victimization (four items) were measured using the Illinois Bullying and Victimization Scales. A LASSO-regularized ordinal cross-lagged panel network was estimated to examine prospective item-level associations while controlling for age and sex.
RESULTS: Persistency varied across specific perpetration behaviors, whereas all four victimization experiences showed positive autoregressive associations. Cross-lagged associations were observed within and between perpetration and victimization, indicating behavior-specific patterns of transitivity. Being called names showed the highest Out-Strength, whereas contributing to harassment, being hit and pushed, and teasing peers showed relatively high In-Strength.
CONCLUSIONS: Bullying dynamics are behavior-specific. The prospective connections among specific perpetration behaviors and victimization experiences highlight potential points of attention for bullying prevention and intervention. Network-based approaches provide refined insights into the victim-offender overlap and may inform more focused school-based prevention efforts.
